findings.title: Chunked-Encoding chunk footer not validated: arbitrary two bytes accepted after chunk data (request-smuggling enabler)
findings.evidence:
Root cause: ChunkedReader records the two bytes that RFC 7230 requires between chunk-data and the next chunk-size only as a count (`self._bytes_to_discard = 2`, line 197) and then consumes them at lines 163-170 via `buf.maybe_extract_at_most(self._bytes_to_discard)` (line 164) followed by an unconditional `self._bytes_to_discard -= len(data)` (line 167). The extracted bytes are never compared against b'
', so any attacker-chosen footer (e.g. 'XX', '

', or bytes that a different parser would treat as the start of the next chunk header/request) is silently discarded and the message is accepted as well-formed. Reachability: any remote peer that sends a message with `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` reaches this code - the READERS table maps 'chunked' to ChunkedReader (lines 242-246) and Connection.receive_data()/next_event() in _connection.py drive __call__ over attacker-controlled bytes; no local privileges or special configuration are needed. Verified PoC against this exact tree (h11 0.14.0): feeding `POST / HTTP/1.1
Host: x
Transfer-Encoding: chunked

5
helloXX0

` yields Data(b'hello') + EndOfMessage with no error, while the patched h11 0.16.0 raises RemoteProtocolError("malformed chunk footer: bytearray(b'XX') (expected b'
')"). Impact: parser divergence / inconsistent interpretation of HTTP message boundaries (CWE-444). This is the root cause fixed upstream in 0.16.0 as CVE-2025-43859 / GHSA-vqfr-h8mv-ghfj ("Reject certain malformed Transfer-Encoding: chunked bodies that were previously accepted"); per that advisory, exploitation as request smuggling requires an h11-based server to be deployed behind an intermediary with a matching chunked-parsing bug (e.g. a load balancer/proxy that delimits these bytes differently), which is the precondition under which a stream h11 reads as one message is read by the intermediary as another - no end-to-end smuggling is claimed for h11 in isolation.
